title: The Connoisseur's Gold Buying Guide: Understanding 22K vs 24K and BIS Hallmarking
author: Master Gemologist, Pukhraj Jewellers
excerpt: Demystifying gold purities, karats, alloys, and why BIS 916 hallmarking is your sacred guarantee when acquiring gold jewellery.

content.text: Gold has remained humanity's timeless store of emotional and financial value for millennia. However, stepping into a jewellery showroom can often raise fundamental questions regarding purity, making charges, and hallmarking standards.
What is 24 Karat vs 22 Karat Gold?

24 Karat gold is 99.9% pure elementary gold. In its virgin state, 24K gold is inherently ductile and soft, making it unsuitable for intricate wearable jewellery with prongs or filigree. Hence, 24K is primarily cast into investment bullion coins and mint bars.

22 Karat gold contains 91.6% pure gold alloyed with 8.4% reinforcing metals such as silver, zinc, and copper. This 916 formulation achieves the ideal balance of regal warm lustre and tensile resilience necessary for durable bridal sets and necklaces.

Every legitimate gold item sold in India must feature three essential hallmarking laser inscriptions: The BIS triangular logo, the purity grade (such as 22K916 or 18K750), and the unique 6-digit alphanumeric HUID (Hallmark Unique Identification) code. At Pukhraj Jewellers, 100% of our inventory carries official HUID certification.

keyTakeaways: 24K is pure gold best suited for investment bars and coins.
22K (916) offers the supreme standard for handcrafted Indian gold jewellery.
Always verify the 6-digit HUID code using the BIS CARE smartphone app.
Inquire specifically about transparent net gold weight vs stone weight.

title: The Royal Bridal Suite: How to Harmonize Necklines, Lehengas & Heirloom Pieces
author: Bridal Stylist, Pukhraj Jewellers
excerpt: A curated bridal roadmap for balancing chokers, long raani haars, maang tikkas, and naths with your bridal attire.

content.text: An Indian wedding is a sacred tapestry of heritage, family emotion, and visual splendour. The bride's jewellery is not an accessory—it is the crowning glory of her aura and an heirloom passed through generations.
The Layering Principle: Choker + Raani Haar

For deep V or sweetheart lehenga necklines, pair an intricately sculpted high collar choker with an expansive multi-strand Raani Haar. This creates majestic vertical grandeur while highlighting facial symmetry.

If your bridal lehenga features zardozi with antique copper and burnished gold threads, opt for antique matte finish temple jewellery. If your ensemble leans toward pastel silks or diamond sequins, uncut Polki with emerald Meenakari offers radiant contrast.

keyTakeaways: Select your core jewellery pieces before finalizing the neckline of your bridal blouse.
Layer shorter chokers with longer satlada or raani haars for regal proportions.
Prioritize comfort and weight distribution for earrings and headpieces.

title: Heirloom Preservation: How to Clean, Store, and Care for Gold & Polki Jewellery
author: Craftsmanship Studio, Pukhraj Jewellers
excerpt: Practical, safe methods to protect your gold, polki, and diamond jewellery from dulling, scratching, and humidity.

content.text: Gold does not tarnish or oxidize easily, yet everyday exposure to body oils, perfumes, cosmetics, and atmospheric dust can obscure its natural brilliance over time.
The Gentle Home Cleansing Ritual for Solid Gold

Immerse plain solid gold pieces in lukewarm water mixed with a few drops of mild chemical-free soap for 10 minutes. Use a baby toothbrush with ultra-soft bristles to delicately brush corners, rinse with warm filtered water, and pat dry using a microfiber cloth.
Special Care for Polki and Kundan

Never immerse Polki or Kundan jewellery in water! These pieces feature natural foil backings beneath uncut stones that can degrade if moisture seeps inside. Always wipe with a dry soft cloth and store in airtight individual fabric pouches away from moisture.

keyTakeaways: Apply perfumes and hairspray at least 10 minutes before wearing fine jewellery.
Never expose Polki or Kundan to liquid baths or ultrasonic cleaners.
Store each piece in separate velvet-lined slots to prevent abrasion.
